tolerance_html:
mechloop/tolerance/process.py holds, per process, the standard deviations the tolerance verifier built its 3000 simulated machines with. The sheets hold the fabricator to +/-2 standard deviations of the same figures, so a batch of parts inside the drawing tolerance is the population that was simulated. A part AT the limit everywhere is worse than what was simulated: the limits are not a licence to sit on them.

printing_html:
• Printer assumed by the manufacture verifier: build volume (220.0, 220.0, 220.0), nozzle 0.4 mm, layer 0.2 (the verifier default: the design does not declare one) mm.
  • Orientation: pinned per part in the design (print_up), listed below; the STL is already turned so the bed face is on Z = 0.
  • Walls and infill: not declared by the design. The verifier's mass and time estimate used: estimate: 1.2 mm walls, 20% infill, 5 mm3/s, no support material counted.
  • The FEA load cases treat every printed part as solid, isotropic material. A part printed at 20 % infill is not the part that was analysed. For the parts with a load case (), print solid or accept that the factor of safety is unverified.
  • No threads in plastic, no heat-set inserts: every screw in a printed part runs into a steel nut (captive pockets and slots are in the models).
  • Printed clearance holes are drawn at ISO 273 medium + 0.2 mm FDM allowance (M2.5 3.1, M3 3.6, M4 4.7, M5 5.7, M6 6.8; +0.3 and a teardrop or flat top for a hole whose axis lies in the build plane): vertical holes print undersize. Starting values: print a coupon of M3 holes 3.4 to 3.8 in 0.1 mm steps on the printer that will make the parts, then set the allowance and the slicer's hole compensation (docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md). Bearing seats and insert pockets are drawn to their own figures.

criteria.value: target: direct drive, at most 0.4 kg moving in X: 0.360 kg on the X guide block, block included

criteria.label: Belt clamp
criteria.value: x_belt_pull: factor of safety 18.6 (need 3); peak 10.39 MPa; deflection 0.007 mm

criteria.label: Nozzle-to-bed gap scatter
criteria.value: 99 % of builds within ±1.23 mm; biggest contributors: x_beam / x_rail, tool_plate / x_carriage, bed_magnet / bed_plate

criteria.label: Probe
criteria.value: the bed probe switches before the nozzle touches for every unit, and over-travel ends short of its face: nozzle 2.00 .. 4.00 mm above the bed when the probe switches

criteria.label: Lead screws
criteria.value: three T8×2 screws on one closed belt from one motor; self-locking Z lead screws self-locking (efficiency < 0.5): efficiency 0.35

criteria.label: Load case nut_thrust
criteria.value: nut_thrust: factor of safety 22.6 (need 3); peak 12.19 MPa; deflection 0.029 mm

criteria.label: Rail and screw tops
criteria.value: Z rails and lead screws end below the top back extrusion (no rubbing): rail tops 304.0, screw tops 336.0 / 336.0 / 336.0 vs extrusion underside 384.0

criteria.label: Bed level as built
criteria.value: bed out of level 99th percentile 1.39 mm before levelling; three-screw Z, one guide block per rail

criteria.label: Payload
criteria.value: payload_x3_on_bed: nozzle deflection 1.56 µm under the load case

criteria.label: Heated bed +60 K
criteria.value: bed_heated_60K: largest thermal growth 0.413 mm (bonded where parts touch; sliding contacts (normal load only, free in their plane, frictionless): bed_magnet / bed ('magnet'), bed_thumb_1_washer / z_deck ('sliding free: held against the deck's underside by the spring's preload, slips as the plate grows'), bed_thumb_2_washer / z_deck ('sliding free: held against the deck's underside by the spring's preload, slips as the plate grows'))

criteria.label: Bed support result
criteria.value: v10: the Z motors may tilt the carrier by at least 3 x the routine height error before a guide block, a flexure web or a nut seat reaches its limit, and every nut stays seated over the routine error; the thumb nuts' range covers what the motors may not: one Z motor may stand 1.24 mm out of the plane of the other two (0.97 mm across the print area) before the first limit: nut seats: 4.55 mrad of rocking (z_nut); per screw z_nut 1.24, z_nut_fl 1.26, z_nut_fr 1.26 mm; limits for the governing screw: nut seats: 4.55 mrad of rocking 1.24 mm; z_carriage_left: static moment and load / 3 1.72 mm; z_ca

criteria.label: Bed reaches nozzle
criteria.value: bed can reach the nozzle: 0-0.2 mm gap at the top of the print height: nozzle tip is 0.10 mm above the bed surface with the bed 180 mm up

criteria.label: Mains
criteria.value: Live terminals under 3 printed covers (mains_cover_relay, mains_cover_psu, mains_cover_inlet), each held by screws into inserts.

criteria.label: Board
criteria.value: CTRL-OCTOPUS-V1.1: BIGTREETECH Octopus V1.1 control board (8 driver sockets)

parts.name: carriage_plate_left
parts.desc: Carriage plate (left): one of three identical flat 1.6 mm 6061 plates. Its top 20 mm is bolted to the 2020 square's outer face (two M5, T-nuts); its bottom carries the guide block z_carriage_left (four M3 x 5 into the block's own threads). The 30 mm web between them is a flexure: stiff along the wall, soft square to it (251 N/mm), so this block locates the carrier along the wall only and a rail that is not exactly parallel, or a carrier that has grown warm, bends the web instead of loading the block.

parts.name: carriage_plate_right
parts.desc: Carriage plate (right): one of three identical flat 1.6 mm 6061 plates. Its top 20 mm is bolted to the 2020 square's outer face (two M5, T-nuts); its bottom carries the guide block z_carriage_right (four M3 x 5 into the block's own threads). The 30 mm web between them is a flexure: stiff along the wall, soft square to it (251 N/mm), so this block locates the carrier along the wall only and a rail that is not exactly parallel, or a carrier that has grown warm, bends the web instead of loading the block.

parts.name: carriage_plate_rear
parts.desc: Carriage plate (rear): one of three identical flat 1.6 mm 6061 plates. Its top 20 mm is bolted to the 2020 square's outer face (two M5, T-nuts); its bottom carries the guide block z_carriage_rear (four M3 x 5 into the block's own threads). The 30 mm web between them is a flexure: stiff along the wall, soft square to it (251 N/mm), so this block locates the carrier along the wall only and a rail that is not exactly parallel, or a carrier that has grown warm, bends the web instead of loading the block.

parts.name: nut_plate
parts.desc: Laser-cut 6061 nut plate under the carrier's square. How the bed is lifted: the T8 brass nut z_nut rides lead screw leadscrew. Its 22 mm flange is under this 6.35 mm plate, which is bolted under the 2020 square's member sq_rear (two M5 from below into T-nuts), and its 10.2 mm barrel goes up through the plate's 16.6 mm hole. The carrier's weight rests on the flange, so when the screw turns the nut climbs it and lifts the plate, the square, the deck and the bed. The M2.5 pin screw nut_pin (through a 5 mm aluminium sleeve, fixed in the flange) sits in a radial slot in the plate: it stops the nut turning with the screw while letting it float 2.8 mm sideways. The nut is captive: the laser-cut keeper nut_keeper, bolted 0.1 mm under the flange on two M3 through-bolts and spacers, stops the plate lifting off it. The three nut plates are one shape, as are the three keepers.

parts.name: nut_plate_fl
parts.desc: Laser-cut 6061 nut plate under the carrier's square. How the bed is lifted: the T8 brass nut z_nut_fl rides lead screw leadscrew_fl. Its 22 mm flange is under this 6.35 mm plate, which is bolted under the 2020 square's member sq_left (two M5 from below into T-nuts), and its 10.2 mm barrel goes up through the plate's 16.6 mm hole. The carrier's weight rests on the flange, so when the screw turns the nut climbs it and lifts the plate, the square, the deck and the bed. The M2.5 pin screw nut_pin_fl (through a 5 mm aluminium sleeve, fixed in the flange) sits in a radial slot in the plate: it stops the nut turning with the screw while letting it float 2.8 mm sideways. The nut is captive: the laser-cut keeper nut_keeper_fl, bolted 0.1 mm under the flange on two M3 through-bolts and spacers, stops the plate lifting off it. The three nut plates are one shape, as are the three keepers.

parts.desc: Microswitch endstop board (lever switch, OMRON D2F-01L type: gold contacts, for logic-level current)
parts.model_source: FreeCAD-library (community, CC-BY 3.0): Microswitch_SPDT_Horizontal_L.step (D2F-size lever switch) on a generated 20 x 12.5 mm board
parts.bom_basis: catalogue level 'partial': switch figures (body, operating position 6.8 +/-1.5 mm, overtravel 0.55 mm min, movement differential 0.5 mm max, operating force 0.78 N max) are OMRON's D2F data sheet. Buy the gold-contact low-current type (D2F-01L): a general-purpose D2F needs 100 mA at 5 V as its minimum load, a 3.3 V logic input with a pull-up draws far less; D2F-01 needs 1 mA. The 20 x 12.5 mm carrier board is generated, not a known bought module: its terminal row (0.9 mm below the body bottom, 2.62 mm through the board) is kept as drawn. OMRON's right-angled terminals (-A) would be 2.6 +/-0.2 mm below the body bottom and 1.5 mm through a 1.6 mm board: re-check the three terminal holes once the bought module is known

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Bed probe on a thin spring-steel sheet: sensing distance unverified
open_items.known: Every probe figure (z_offset 3.0 mm, range [2.0, 4.0], face window [0.574, 3.426] mm) assumes the sensor switches at 5.0 mm, the maker's figure for a 1 mm iron target. The target here is 235 x 235 mm PEI spring-steel print sheet, held on bed_magnet by magnetism alone: lift it off to remove prints., 0.4 mm (a catalogue part) on its magnetic base. Basis recorded by the report: OMRON E2E data sheet CSM_E2E_DS_E_12_4: 5 mm +/-10 % on the standard iron target.
open_items.check: COMMISSIONING.md step B1 with the real sensor, sheet and magnet BEFORE ordering anything else; pass window there

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Mains side: printed hoods only, one bonded extrusion, not certified
open_items.known: Open frame; the inlet's rear, the relay module and the supply terminals are under printed hoods (mains_cover_relay, mains_cover_relay_screw_0, mains_cover_relay_screw_0_washer, mains_cover_relay_screw_0_nwasher, mains_cover_relay_screw_0_nut, mains_cover_relay_screw_1, mains_cover_relay_screw_1_washer, mains_cover_relay_screw_1_nwasher, mains_cover_relay_screw_1_nut, mains_cover_psu, mains_cover_psu_screw_0, mains_cover_psu_screw_0_washer, mains_cover_psu_screw_0_nwasher, mains_cover_psu_screw_0_nut, mains_cover_psu_screw_1, mains_cover_psu_screw_1_washer, mains_cover_psu_screw_1_nwasher, mains_cover_psu_screw_1_nut, mains_cover_inlet, mains_cover_inlet_screw_0, mains_cover_inlet_screw_0_washer, mains_cover_inlet_screw_0_nwasher, mains_cover_inlet_screw_0_nut, mains_cover_inlet_screw_1, mains_cover_inlet_screw_1_washer, mains_cover_inlet_screw_1_nwasher, mains_cover_inlet_screw_1_nut) that are open where the wires enter: touch protection depends on fully insulated receptacles and the hoods being fitted. The model earths the supply and one extrusion; everything else relies on anodised joints. The supply has a 115 / 230 V selector that must be set by hand.
open_items.check: WIRING.md mains section; continuity test E1; a competent person signs off the mains side

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Corner-bracket screws have no washer on the casting's slot
open_items.known: Each of the 64 bracket legs takes a bare M5 x 8 cap-screw head on the casting's 6 mm slot: 27 % of the seat the head has on a round hole (ratings warning). Washers do not fit: with one under each head the two heads in a bracket collide inside the slots. The guideline 'washers on slots' is therefore NOT met at the brackets.
open_items.check: use flanged button-head screws ISO 7380-2 M5 x 8 (flange about 11.5 mm; not in the catalogue, not checked) or brackets with round holes (Misumi HBLFSN5 has 5.2 mm holes); decide before buying

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: Screw lengths in T-slots rest on Misumi's catalogue drawings, without tolerances
open_items.known: Slot 6.0 mm deep with a 2.0 mm lip (HFS5 series), T-nut HNTAJ5 3.2 mm high with a 2.4 mm body under the lips: read from the 2019 US catalogue (copies in vendor_docs/). The drawings give no tolerances; 0.5 mm is kept between a screw's tip and the slot floor. If an extrusion of another make is bought, its slot may be shallower: on the other 2020 section on file (5.3 mm deep) 80 of the 156 T-slot screws would end closer than 0.5 mm to the floor (docs/PRINTER_V10_1.md).
open_items.check: buy Misumi HFS5-2020 and HNTAJ5-5 / HNTAJ5-3, or measure the slot depth and lip of what is bought, put the figures in mechloop/parts/vendor/tslot_2020_hardware.json and re-run verify

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: The X rail is a cut-to-length part
open_items.known: HIWIN MGNR12R cut to 288 mm (11 holes, 19 mm end distances): not a stock length. HIWIN's catalogue allows any length to 2000 mm; resellers that cut to order were found only in search snippets, and one warns that a cut piece can come 2 to 3 mm short. Every millimetre the rail is short is a millimetre less than 5 mm between the X block and the rail's end at one end of the travel, not a millimetre of travel.
open_items.check: order 288 +0 / -1 mm with the block; if a stock 300 mm rail is cut at home, cut it with an abrasive disc and deburr, and check the block passes the cut end

open_items.rank_label: would stop the build (or is a safety matter)
open_items.title: The bed mesh does not reach the whole print area
open_items.known: The probe is 34.5 mm behind the nozzle and is kept 12 mm inside the sheet's edge: the front 34.5 mm, 9.3 mm at each side and 1.75 mm at the rear of the 229.6 x 214.5 mm print area are never measured; the mesh holds its nearest value there. A probe with no offset is not possible with this sensor (docs/PRINTER_V10.md, 'Proposal A').
